svg.text: Option C: Passport as the front end for Homegate, your homeserver and your identity
Onboarding and profile management move out of pubky.app. Sign-in as in A.1; Passport gets a child grant for identity management.
Already have a pubky? Import it
Verify to get 1 GB of storage
Grant only, load it to sign
your identity, with a child grant
3 ID token, SMS code, or payment
5 sign up with the code (an invite code goes straight here)
key: this browser, Ring, or grant only
6 signed parent grant (or from Ring or Bitkit)
10 Log in, like any suite app
+ Onboarding and profile management leave pubky.app, and every app gets them.
+ Apps only link Passport. Users can pick their own Passport instance in the SDK.
+ No lock-in: each identity picks its Homegate, or a homeserver with no Homegate.
+ Every Homegate method in one place: SSO, SMS, Lightning, invite code.
+ Identity management works for every identity, also when the key is in Ring or Bitkit.
+ Users choose how much the browser holds: the key, or only a grant.
− Homegate must derive Passport's current wrapping key, or existing backups can't be unlocked.
− Each Homegate needs its own SSO setup (Google client, Apple Services ID).
− Sign-in and sign-up options depend on the chosen Homegate, so screens differ per provider.
− SSO backup needs a Homegate. Own homeserver without one: import or Mobile Signer only.
− Backups are bound to the Passport address that made them. Another instance needs a recovery file
− Passport grows: SMS, Lightning and profile screens move in from pubky.app.
− Moving a key to Ring needs a hand-over format that Ring imports.
− Grant-only SSO identities need an SSO sign-in each time Passport has to sign.
− The SDK needs a setting for the Passport address.
